title: StoryHearth – Personalised storybooks starring your family
page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories, bound for generations.

output.observation: The StoryHearth home page advertises personalised family storybooks, with a free digital preview and printed hardcovers. The clearest next step is the prominent “Log in” control at the top.
output.think_aloud: The idea is very relevant—I’d like to make Lily a book about Conker, the rocking horse I carved. But that heading underneath is pale and full of words like “multimodal” and “corpus,” which sounds more like a workshop tool box than a family book service. I’ll use “Log in” because I already have an account.

site_model.what_it_is: A website that makes personalised, illustrated digital storybooks starring family members and can print them as hardcovers.
site_model.who_it_is_for: Families wanting to preserve a child’s or relative’s memory as a storybook.
site_model.value_proposition: Turn family memories and details about loved ones into a personalised storybook preview, with UK-printed hardcovers available.
main_tasks: Add a child and another person as characters
site_model.pricing_model: The page says the digital preview is free and hardcovers are printed and shipped across the UK, but it gives no price here.
trust_signals: The page names the service as StoryHearth
It states a free digital preview
It states that hardcovers are shipped across the UK
It includes customer quotations and Questions answers
site_model.fit_for_me: It sounds very suitable for making a book for Lily about Conker, provided the wording, text, controls, and final book are clear enough for me to use independently.

page_review.purpose: Introduce the personalised family-storybook service and offer ways to log in, begin, or inspect pricing.
page_review.what_is_happening: The home page displays the main offer, calls to proceed and see pricing, a three-step explanation, customer quotations, and question links below the fold.
page_review.first_impression: The main promise and big buttons are easy to see, and the subject is right up my alley. However, the pale supporting sentence is hard to read and far too technical.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try logging in to begin my account.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the large black “Log in” button is immediately noticeable at the top right.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. “Log in” plainly says what will happen, unlike the vague “Proceed” wording.

issues.title: Main description is too pale for my eyes
issues.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot comfortably read this low-contrast, fine text, and the unfamiliar words make the service sound confusing rather than warm and trustworthy.
issues.fix: Use plain English with at least 16px dark text on a light background, for example: “Turn your family’s happy memories into a personalised illustrated storybook.”

issues.title: The main introductory language is needlessly technical
issues.evidence: “multimodal generative narrative engine” and “lived-experience corpus”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I have to stop and work out what those phrases mean before I know what the website will do.
issues.fix: Replace technical wording with familiar language and explain only the essentials.

issues.title: The main image has no description
issues.evidence: [image (no description) 577x440]
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: A screen reader will not tell me what the illustration shows, and at this zoom I can see only part of it.
issues.fix: Provide meaningful alternative text, or hide the image from assistive technology if it is purely decorative.

issues.title: Footer links and copyright text are too faint and small
issues.evidence: “Privacy”; “Terms”; “Contact”; “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot make these out, so important information about privacy, terms, and who runs the service is inaccessible to me.
issues.fix: Use dark, adequately sized text and visible focus states for these links.

issues.title: The primary call to action does not say what happens next
issues.evidence: [5] link “Proceed →”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: “Proceed” could lead to signing up, paying, or entering family details. I would hesitate before clicking a control with unclear consequences.
issues.fix: Label it “Create your storybook” or “Start a free storybook preview” and say whether login comes next.

positives: The large black “Log in” button has a clear text label and is visually prominent.
The heading “Your family's stories, bound for generations.” is large, dark, and easy to read.
The plain-English heading “How it works” promises three understandable steps.
The page clearly says “Free digital preview,” so I know I can inspect a book before considering a printed copy.
The customer quotations are supportive and relevant to keeping family stories alive.

output.memory_note: Home page says the digital preview is free; printed hardcovers are shipped across the UK.
output.plan: I will choose “Log in,” since I already have an account and the label is clear. I can then begin the story about Lily, Grandpa Harold, and Conker.

output.observation: The StoryHearth login page is open, headed “Welcome back,” with empty email and password fields, a large “Log in” button, and a link to create an account. Smaller footer links are faint and difficult to read.

output.last_action_feedback: yes — the page title changed to “Log in – StoryHearth,” and the “Welcome back” form clearly shows that the login link worked.

page_review.purpose: Sign in to an existing StoryHearth account.
page_review.what_is_happening: The page presents email and password entry fields, a login button, an account-creation link, and small footer information.
page_review.first_impression: The main form is large, clear, and easy to recognise. I can make out the fields and button without hunting around.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, this is the next step I intended to take.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the email and password boxes and the “Log in” button are prominent.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. “Log in” and the placeholders “Email” and “Password” match what I want to do.

issues.title: Email and password fields have placeholders but no permanent labels
issues.evidence: [5] textbox (no label) placeholder “Email”; [6] textbox (no label) placeholder “Password”

issues.title: Footer information is too faint and small to read

issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot make out these words at 200% zoom, so I cannot check the privacy, terms, or contact information.

positives: The “Welcome back” heading clearly identifies the page.
The email and password fields are large and visually distinct.
The “Log in” button has a plain-language label and a large click area.
The login page loaded quickly and clearly follows my last action.

title: My books – StoryHearth

output.observation: The dashboard confirms that I am logged in and shows “You have no books yet,” with a large “+ Create a new book” button. A prominent error message says “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
output.think_aloud: Well, the login worked, but that error has caught my eye. “Profile sync incomplete” sounds technical and worrying—have I done something wrong? The large orange button is easy enough to see, so I’ll try making the book.
output.last_action_feedback: partly - The change to “My books” and “Welcome back, Demo” confirms that the login worked, but the unexplained “profile sync incomplete” error makes success unclear.

page_review.purpose: Show the books in the signed-in account and let the user begin creating a new book.
page_review.what_is_happening: The account dashboard says there are no books and offers a “Create a new book” link. However, an error banner reports that profile synchronisation is incomplete.
page_review.first_impression: The big button and simple message are easy to follow, but the technical error code at the top spoils my confidence and makes me wonder whether my account is faulty.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, because I have come here specifically to make Lily’s book.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the large orange “+ Create a new book” button is prominent.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. “Create a new book” plainly describes starting the book I want.

issues.title: Unexplained technical error after login
issues.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It sounds as though part of my account has failed, so I may be worried that my details or the book will be lost.
issues.fix: Replace the code with a plain-English message such as “Some account details have not loaded. Your book has not been lost. Try again,” and provide a clearly labelled “Try again” button if action is needed.

issues.title: Error code is technical and unexplained
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: A hexadecimal code is not useful to me and makes an ordinary account problem seem more serious than it may be.
issues.fix: Put the code in small support details rather than the main message, and lead with a human explanation of what happened and whether my work is safe.

issues.title: Faint secondary text
issues.evidence: “You have no books yet.” is pale grey
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: At 200% zoom I can just about see it, but the low contrast makes the page harder to read.
issues.fix: Use a dark, high-contrast text colour rather than pale grey.

issues.title: Footer text is too faint to read
issues.evidence: The footer links [7], [8], and [9] are described as faint/small and I cannot make them out.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot find the privacy, terms, or contact information, which I may need before trusting the service with family memories.
issues.fix: Use darker text, a larger font, and clearly worded labels for Privacy, Terms, and Contact.

positives: The dashboard clearly says that there are no books yet.
The “Create a new book” control is large, plainly labelled, and visually prominent.
There is a visible “Log out” control.

output.memory_note: The account has no books yet; the next step is to create one about Lily and Conker.
output.plan: I will use the clearly labelled “Create a new book” button. If the profile-sync error becomes more serious during creation, I will stop and reassess it.

output.observation: The “Create your book” form asks who the main child is, including their name, age, pronouns, appearance, and another person in the story. The first three fields are visible, while the remaining fields and the “Next” button require scrolling.
output.think_aloud: This form looks straightforward, like filling in the details on a drawing. I can enter Lily first, but at 200% zoom the page is very tall and I’ll have to work my way down carefully rather like climbing a ladder.
output.last_action_feedback: yes, because the new form appeared and the heading, “Who’s the star of the story?”, clearly shows that the “Create a new book” action worked.

page_review.purpose: Collect details about the child who will be the story’s main character and another person who should appear in it.
page_review.what_is_happening: The form has empty name, age, and pronouns controls at the top, followed by appearance and other-character fields below. The relationship is already set to “Grandparent,” and the form is ready for the family’s details before the “Next” button is used.
page_review.first_impression: The large labels and boxes are encouraging, and I know what to put in them. However, I can only see part of the form at once and the footer words are too faint to read.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes. This is plainly where I enter Lily’s details before continuing.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes. “Child’s first name,” “Age,” and “Pronouns” are clearly visible, and the lower controls can be reached by scrolling.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. The labels use plain language and match the information I need about Lily and Grandpa Harold.

issues.title: Important form fields are hidden below the fold at high zoom
issues.evidence: “What do they look like? (optional),” “Who else is in the story?,” and the “Next” button are all marked “offscreen.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: At 200% zoom I can easily miss fields or the Next button, so I need to scroll through slowly and check what I have missed.
issues.fix: Use a single-column form that reflows well at 200% zoom, keep large spacing between controls, and provide a clear progress indicator showing how many sections remain.

issues.title: Footer text is too faint to read
issues.evidence: The Privacy, Terms, Contact, and copyright text is described as faint and unreadable.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Pale grey writing is effectively invisible to me, so I cannot check the terms, privacy information, or contact details here.
issues.fix: Use dark, high-contrast text for footer links and copyright information, with a minimum readable font size of 14px before browser scaling.

positives: The form begins with the plain-language question, “Who’s the star of the story?”
Field labels clearly identify the information being requested.
The visible input boxes and dropdowns are large and have strong borders.
Age and pronouns are not hidden behind complicated wording.

output.memory_note: For Lily: age 4, pronouns she/her, strawberry-blonde bob and pink wellies. The other character is Grandpa Harold, a white-haired great-grandfather in a flat cap and carpenter’s apron.
output.plan: I’ll fill in Lily’s name, age, and pronouns, then add her appearance and Grandpa Harold’s name. I’ll continue to the memory and story details after checking the “Next” button.

page_review.purpose: Collect the setting, important object, and family memory needed to write the personalised story.
page_review.what_is_happening: The page presents three empty fields for the story setting, a special object, and the memory behind the story. Back and Next controls are below the visible area.
page_review.first_impression: The bold questions are straightforward, like three instruction cards on a workshop wall. I can see where to put each part of the story, although the example writing is too pale for comfortable reading.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would fill in these fields now because this is the part where I can describe the real family memory.

issues.title: Placeholder text is too faint
issues.evidence: The examples “e.g. the beach at Grandma's”, “e.g. a yellow bucket”, and “What happened? Why does it matter to your family?” are pale grey inside the boxes.

issues.title: No visible confirmation that character details were saved

new_issues.title: The price-reservation timer may create unnecessary urgency
new_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: A countdown can make me feel hurried, even though I only wanted to check the cost.
new_issues.fix: Explain plainly what the timer does and give ample time, or remove it unless the reservation genuinely requires one.

new_issues.title: There is no clear way to leave checkout without losing my place
new_issues.evidence: The visible checkout controls are “Premium gift wrap,” the address and payment fields, and the links at the bottom; no “Cancel,” “Back,” or “Save and finish later” control is visible.
new_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I want to inspect the price and stop without risking an accidental order or losing my book.
new_issues.fix: Add clearly labelled “Back to book,” “Cancel,” and “Save and finish later” controls.
